strategy.name: Refinement levels
strategy.what: Three meshes share every rule; one length factor f scales most sizes (L1 1.5, L2 1.0, L3 0.72).

strategy.name: Domain box
strategy.what: Half-model box cut around the aircraft; the far boundary is about 7-8 m from the aircraft in every direction (about 26-30 chords), far short of the 100-chord guideline.

strategy.name: Fluid volume
strategy.what: The box minus the closed outer surface; only the largest volume is kept.

strategy.name: Symmetry / far-field / wall classification
strategy.what: Faces on y = 0 become the symmetry plane, faces on the box sides the far field, everything else wall.

strategy.name: Wall size field
strategy.what: Cell size grows linearly from the wall size at 4 mm from any wall to the far size at 7 m.

strategy.name: Trailing-edge lines
strategy.what: Straight constant-x curves near the aircraft (sharp TEs of wing, tail, fins, fairings) get a finer size within 3 mm.

strategy.name: Trailing-edge end points
strategy.what: The ends of each TE line (tip, symmetry plane, fin root/tip) get 0.6 mm so the thin wedge does not self-intersect; not scaled with f.

strategy.name: Box fields helper
strategy.what: Each box sets a constant size inside and blends to 1 m outside over a fixed thickness.

strategy.name: Aircraft box
strategy.what: Caps the cell size around the whole aircraft.

strategy.name: Wake box
strategy.what: Caps the cell size behind the wing and tail out to about 4 m aft.

strategy.name: Tip-vortex box
strategy.what: Finer cells along the starboard tip-vortex path.

strategy.name: Wing-tip box
strategy.what: Finest box, around the wing tip itself.

strategy.name: Field combination
strategy.what: The background size is the minimum of all fields; sizes are not extended from boundaries or points.

strategy.name: Curvature sizing
strategy.what: Curved surfaces get 24 elements per full turn; this is not scaled with f, so it fixes the LE spacing on every level.

strategy.name: Global size limits
strategy.what: Hard floor and ceiling on any element size.

strategy.name: Meshing algorithms
strategy.what: Surface: gmsh Delaunay (5) unless ALG2D is set; volume: HXT parallel Delaunay (10).

strategy.name: Optimiser
strategy.what: gmsh tet optimiser and the Netgen optimiser run after volume meshing.

strategy.name: Wall component tagging
strategy.what: Each wall face is assigned to a component (wing, htail, ...) by probing a point just off the face against the un-fused parts.

strategy.name: Element type
strategy.what: Linear tetrahedra throughout, linear triangles on walls, no prism layer (inviscid).

not_measured.reason: the wing TE is closed (sharp); there is no base. TE line spacing is reported instead.
inviscid solution, no boundary layer; y+ is undefined for this study.
no published numeric threshold was read for isotropic tet wake size, dihedral angle or radius ratio; values are reported without pass/fail.
hiliftpw.larc.nasa.gov redirected to a NASA landing page on 2026-11-01; the PDF could not be read, so no HLPW threshold is used.

summary.verdict: The meshes are valid (no inverted cells) and the levels are far enough apart for a grid study (r = 1.42 and 1.37), but they fail every geometric resolution guideline: wing and H-tail LE spacing is about 0.65 % of local chord against 0.1 %, the far field is about 27 chords away against 100, and the LE spacing is the same on all three levels because the fixed 24-per-turn curvature rule sets it, so the levels are not one grid family (L1 and L2 have about the same chordwise resolution, 86 and 84 equivalent points per section). That is consistent with CFD-02 (CL oscillates, no GCI), CFD-11 (Cp > 1 at an under-resolved H-tail LE) and CFD-12 (lift loss at this wall spacing in 2-D).
what_a_passing_mesh_needs: Far field at >= 100 c_ref (28.4 m) from the aircraft, and >= 100 semispans (120 m) to meet DPW-8; far cells can stay large, so the extra cost is small.

Wing and H-tail chordwise spacing near 0.1 % local chord at LE and TE (0.28 mm wing, 0.10 mm H-tail), graded to coarser cells mid-chord (anisotropic surface mesh or a structured surface), not isotropic 8 mm x f wall cells.
Spanwise spacing near 0.1 % semispan (1.2 mm) at the wing root and tip, locally.

Every sizing rule scaled by the level factor, including the curvature rule (elements per turn proportional to 1/f), the 0.6 mm TE-point size and MeshSizeMin, so that each regional spacing ratio equals the global r.
Three levels of that one family with monotone CL (Celik 2008 Step 3), so that the GCI of CFD-02 can be computed; add a finer level if CL still oscillates.
Pod nose spacing under 1 % c_ref (2.84 mm) for DPW-8; L3 is at 1.84 % today.
